title: Midweek platform standup + deep-dive: control plane, routing, auth, quotas
content:
Attendees: Maya (owner), Ethan, Lina, Omar, Sophie, plus small async notes from Kai and Quincy who were on-call.

Purpose: midweek sync to (1) surface any regression or SLA drift in the control plane, (2) reconcile routing anomalies from yesterday's canary, (3) check status on auth token rotation rollout, and (4) review quota refactor spike progress. This is more of a working-standup + deep-dive, not a polished status update.

High-level summary:
- SLA: eu-west-1 p99 latency for control-plane registration spiked to ~820ms between 03:10–04:20 UTC. Root cause appears to be a cascade from a slow KV eviction job competing with the allocator reconciler (see PLAT-8421). No customer-facing impact observed (routing fallback kicked in).
- Routing: Canary for route-based shard selection (ROUTE-997) showed a 0.9% increase in 5xx for low-traffic pools; investigation points to timeout threshold mismatch when the allocator replies with partial-placement.
- Auth: v2 token rotation rollout completed to 60% of traffic in prod; a small number (~0.02%) of requests failed with 401 due to clock skew on a legacy batch worker - patch landed and will be backfilled.
- Quotas: quota-refactor spike (design doc linked) is on-track; Lina has a working prototype that reuses token-bucket state across instance restarts. Need one more test for burst reclaim behavior.

Detailed notes / timeline:
03:05 UTC - Monitoring alert: control-plane-registry p99 > 700ms. Kai triaged and escalated to control plane on-call.
03:10 - 03:40 - Correlation observed between registry GC window (kv-evictor job) and allocator reconciliation lag. Stack traces show a hot lock on kv-store shard 11.
03:40 - Deployed temporary mitigation: reduce kv-evictor batch size from 2k -> 200 keys, reduced lock contention; p99 dropped back toward baseline ~210ms by 04:10.
04:20 - Follow-up: scheduled controlled rollout of kv-evictor tuned parameters to other clusters.

Routing canary notes:
- Canary rollout (ROUTE-997) to 5% completed yesterday. Low-traffic pools saw a small spike in 5xx at approximately the same window as control-plane spike. Hypothesis: when allocator responds slower, the new shard-selection flow times out faster than the legacy flow and retries to fallback tier, generating transient 5xx.
- Action: Increase route selection timeout from 400ms -> 900ms in canary, and instrument allocation-response latency histogram for correlation. Ethan will push change and run another 2hr canary.

Auth / token rotation:
- v2 rotation: using KMS-signed short-lived tokens (90s TTL) for inter-service auth. Rollout metrics: 60% of traffic; failed requests were concentrated on legacy batch-workers with old system time.
- Omar patched the worker images and scheduled a rolling restart. Backfill plan: reprocess ~14k stalled jobs over the weekend with throttling.
- TODO: add clock-skew detector to healthcheck and surface in SRE runbook. Owner: Omar. ETA: 2026-12-07.

Quotas / token-bucket refactor:
- Spike progress: Lina's prototype persists bucket state in the control plane so ephemeral frontends can recover quota after crashes. Early test shows ~15% lower rejected-ratio under simulated churn.
- Remaining unknown: reclaim policy when global pool is exhausted and frontends submit in-flight reservations. Need a deterministic tie-breaker: options are (a) timestamp-first, (b) priority-weighted, (c) randomized backoff.
- Decision lean: prefer priority-weighted with small randomized jitter to avoid thundering herd. Work item created: PLAT-8499.

Open problems & questions:
- Are there other background jobs (besides kv-evictor) that hold the same shard-level lock and could cause similar cross-cutting latency? Action: run a lock-holder audit across controlplane repo. Owner: Maya. Due: 2026-12-10.
- Do we have sufficient observability to map allocator partial-placement events to route selection decisions? Ethan to add a correlation id through the stack and capture traces for 2% of requests.
- Can the quota prototype safely handle cross-region consistency during network partitions? Lina to write a short spec and failure-mode matrix.

Action items (owners / due dates):
- Ethan: Increase route-selection timeout in canary, add allocation-response histograms, run 2hr canary. Due: 2026-12-04.
- Lina: Add failure-mode matrix for quota-refactor and propose tie-breaker algorithm doc. Due: 2026-12-09.
- Omar: Add clock-skew detector to healthchecks, finish rolling restart and backfill plan. Due: 2026-12-07.
- Maya: Run lock-holder audit for controlplane and produce a short remediation plan. Due: 2026-12-10.
- Sophie: Schedule a short postmortem if control-plane p99 shows another >700ms incident within 7 days. Due: follow-up on incident recurrence.

Notes for next standup / follow-ups:
- If canary passes with larger timeout, consider applying route timeout increase to prod with staged rollout.
- If kv-evictor tuning is safe, propose a safer default for all clusters and codify as a runtime config with cluster-level overrides.
- Revisit quota tie-breaker design before merging spike into feature branch (do not merge until tie-breaker is agreed).

Misc (notes-to-self / raw fragments):
- "kv-evictor reduced batch size: saw immediate p99 win - may indicate lock granularity bug in shard map"
- "trace-id correlation missing between allocator -> router when fallback path used"
- add small synthetic test that simulates allocator slowness + routing canary to reproduce 5xx condition locally

Meeting close: next sync 2026-12-04 standup; will share short status on canary and patch results.

References / quick links: PLAT-8421 (kv-evictor contention), ROUTE-997 (shard-selection canary), PLAT-8499 (quota tie-breaker), PR: controlplane#3142 (kv-evictor batch size tweak).

End of notes.
